entries.title: Towards Scale-Up Networking: Challenges and Open Questions
entries.abstract: The rapid growth of AI models and the widespread use of distributed training and inference have made inter-accelerator communication a critical system bottleneck. Scale-up fabrics address this bottleneck by combining high per-accelerator bandwidth with low and predictable latency over tightly coupled accelerator domains. However, the appropriate topology, protocol mechanisms, communication semantics, and system integration remain actively debated. We analyze the critical-path communication generated by parallelism strategies and derive the resulting requirements for domain scale, per-accelerator bandwidth, and collective completion latency. We then use these requirements as a framework to examine representative proprietary and open scale-up fabrics, revealing how their physical interconnects, topologies, protocols, and semantics make different trade-offs among performance, scalability, compatibility, and implementation cost. Moreover, based on this analysis and discussions with industry experts, we identify challenges and open problems in physical interconnects and switching, efficient communication, semantics, resource sharing and heterogeneous device interconnection. This paper provides a requirement-driven foundation for analyzing current scale-up fabrics and guiding the design of future systems.

entries.title: RouterWeave: A Unified Observation Layer for Cross-Platform Activity Analysis via Home Routers
entries.abstract: Smart homes bring together devices from different operating systems and vendor ecosystems, but each platform reports activity only for the devices and features it supports, leaving gaps in household-wide activity monitoring. Interoperability standards such as Matter and software integrations connect and control supported devices, yet vendor restrictions and licensing barriers limit access to their data, while hardware constraints hinder integration. Our key insight is that encrypted network traffic provides complementary evidence of activity across platform boundaries. Accordingly, we present RouterWeave, a router-side observation framework that combines cross-platform traffic collection, task-adaptive processing, and unified activity records. These records preserve activity meaning, temporal extent, and source-device attribution while distinguishing discrete operations from sustained activity intervals. We evaluate RouterWeave across four datasets, native execution on a commodity home router, and two novel case studies: cross-platform Screen Time monitoring and appliance energy estimation. RouterWeave achieves 94.41% macro-F1 on application activities and 97.46% on IoT operations, outperforming baselines by up to 20.99 percentage points, while using under 7 MB of router memory per task and supporting 54 concurrent devices within a 5-second update window. In end-to-end case studies, RouterWeave reconstructs 600 Screen Time timelines across Android, iOS, and Windows with 92.15% accuracy (24.84-second mean active-time error over 19-minute averages) and recovers 49 of 55 appliance operations over four days, tracking ON/OFF states with 92.84% agreement and estimating electricity use within a 4.28% error. Together, these results establish the commodity home router as practical infrastructure for whole-home activity sensing. The code is open sourced at https://github.com/naisslab/routerweave.
entries.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures

entries.title: ScaleWire: An End-to-End Scale-Up Ethernet Simulation Framework for LLM Systems
entries.abstract: LLM training and inference rely on scale-up networks for high-bandwidth, low-latency memory-semantic communication among accelerators (XPUs). Ethernet is emerging as an open interconnect for scale-up systems. In Ethernet systems, network-interface (NI) mechanisms across transport, network, and link layers interact, jointly shaping communication performance and on-chip resource requirements. We present ScaleWire, an end-to-end scale-up Ethernet simulation framework for LLM systems. It couples packet-level simulation of cross-layer NI mechanisms with a resource exploration engine that combines analytical estimates and simulation to size on-chip resources. We validate ScaleWire against hardware measurements and nine analytical checks, and evaluate six NI designs across four LLM communication workloads. For DeepSeek-R1 dispatch, NI design choices lead to a 4.5× difference in per-XPU on-chip storage budget. In grid-comparison experiments, the exploration engine uses 6-19% of the simulations required by exhaustive search. Using vLLM prefill traces with kernel times measured on GH200 GPUs, ScaleWire further guides resource provisioning under a completion-time constraint for inference execution. ScaleWire thus helps designers select NI mechanisms and provision on-chip resources to balance communication performance and resource cost.
entries.comment: 7 pages, 8 figures

entries.title: A Brief Overview of Non-Terrestrial Networks (Updated 2026)
entries.abstract: This article extends the 2023 preprint A brief introduction to satellite communications for Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN) (arXiv:2305.04590v1) with a revision of its foundations, tables and state of the art as of 18 November 2026. It revisits propagation, link budgets, spectrum reuse and phased arrays, including corrected equations and numerical examples. Updated tables distinguish operational, launched and planned constellations and compare published fixed-terminal rates with direct-to-device services. The discussion incorporates developments in 3GPP Releases 17–20, commercial LTE-based direct-to-cell services and research towards 6G non-terrestrial networks. Operator announcements are distinguished from independent measurements and future plans. Open challenges include spectrum coordination, Doppler and timing compensation, mobility, capacity, security and the sustainability of low Earth orbit.

entries.title: Software-Defined Internet Integration of Satellite Networks (SDISN)
entries.abstract: This paper proposes SDISN, a software-defined Internet integration of satellite networks. It facilitates the transmission of IP traffic from user terminals (UTs) or Internet nodes over a satellite network with inter-satellite links (ISLs). Gateways (GWs) together with Points of Presence (PoPs) support the transition between the satellite network and the Internet. UTs and GWs connect to the satellite network via serving satellites (SrvSats). As the satellites orbit the Earth at high speed, UTs and GWs frequently change their SrvSats. This causes frequent changes to their reachability, which poses a major challenge for integration. In the proposed solution, GWs and SrvSats encapsulate traffic with forwarding information so that the traffic can be carried over the satellite network towards appropriate SrvSats of UTs or GWs. The forwarding information on the encapsulating nodes is continuously updated by a controller to reflect changed SrvSats and possibly changed topology of the satellite network. Design goals for the proposed architecture were low complexity on satellites, high ability for traffic engineering, and keeping UTs out of the routing system for security and compatibility reasons. UTs may have increased security requirements (ISRs) such that their traffic should be carried within the constellation to avoid non-trusted terrestrial infrastructure. Extensions are proposed to support such ISRs. UTs may obtain either dynamic IP addresses from a nearby GW/PoP wherever they roam or they may obtain static IP addresses from a fixed Home GW/PoP. In the latter case, triangle routing via the Home GW occurs when the UT roams away from the Home GW. As this adds latency to the communication, we investigate architectural extensions for latency reduction. In addition, we show how traffic engineering can be performed in such an architecture with the help of alternate GWs and SrvSats.

entries.title: An LLM-Driven Traffic-Control xApp for Dynamic 5G RAN Intents
entries.abstract: Programmable Radio Access Networks (RANs) enable runtime deployment of traffic-control functions, but selecting the appropriate configuration remains challenging as network conditions and service requirements change over time. Conventional solutions often rely on static rules or learning-based controllers with predefined state and action spaces, limiting their ability to accommodate changing intents. This paper introduces an LLM-driven xApp for traffic control in programmable RANs. The proposed architecture combines operator-defined service intents, runtime E2 interface telemetry, and the currently deployed configuration to generate traffic-management policies without blocking packet forwarding or the processing of incoming E2 measurements during LLM inference. Experiments on an OpenAirInterface 5G environment show that the proposed controller dynamically adapts the traffic-control pipeline to runtime intent changes, achieving an average intent satisfaction ratio of 0.91, compared with 0.52 for a static TC-RAN configuration. When channel conditions degrade, the controller maintains an intent satisfaction ratio of approx. 0.88, compared with approx. 0.4 for the static baseline.

entries.title: Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
entries.abstract: Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. The results show improved service satisfaction at a throughput cost and improved remote-control performance when random contention is replaced by distributed urgency-based arbitration. We finally discuss the open challenges in intent specification, evidence, hardware execution, interoperability, and lifecycle cost, and outline a staged path toward deployment.
entries.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures

entries.title: SimPyWireless: A PHY-Aware Discrete-Event Simulation Framework for Wi-Fi and 5G NR-U Coexistence in the 5 GHz Band
entries.abstract: The growing demand from heterogeneous wireless applications with stringent QoS and QoE requirements is increasing pressure on available spectrum resources. Although mmWave and THz bands offer additional capacity, their propagation and hardware limitations make sub-6 GHz unlicensed spectrum, particularly the 5 GHz band, an attractive complementary resource. However, reproducible Wi-Fi/5G NR-U coexistence studies remain limited by the lack of lightweight, open-source, PHY-aware simulation platforms. We present SimPyWireless, a discrete-event simulation framework for Wi-Fi and 5G NR-U coexistence in the 5 GHz unlicensed band. The framework integrates shared-channel modeling, propagation, interference, SINR, heterogeneous traffic, mobility, and technology-specific channel access, while providing modular support for externally trained AI/ML models. We validate SimPyWireless against an analytical DTMC model and demonstrate expected coexistence behavior under varying contention and mobility conditions. SimPyWireless provides a reproducible and extensible middle ground between analytical modeling and hardware-based experimentation.
entries.comment: 4 pages, 10 figures

entries.title: Benchmarking Open-Source O-RAN and 5G NTN Stacks on Embedded ARM Platforms for Space Payloads
entries.abstract: Regenerative satellite payloads, which host the 5G Next Generation Node B (gNB) onboard instead of transparently relaying the radio signal, are a key building block of the Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) integration that 3GPP started in Release 17. Combining them with the Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) architecture adds software-defined control through RAN Intelligent Controllers (RICs), enabling in-orbit reconfiguration, multi-tenancy, and data-driven radio resource management. Open-source implementations make this vision accessible to research institutions and New Space missions, yet there is little quantitative evidence on how they behave on the embedded processors that a satellite can actually carry. This paper presents an out-of-the-box experimental benchmark of two open-source gNB stacks (i.e., OpenAirInterface/Duranta and srsRAN/OCUDU), and two Near-Real-Time RICs (i.e., the ORAN-SC Near-RT RIC and FlexRIC). All components are deployed on an ARMv8 platform representative of the processing units used in small-satellite payloads, driving a USRP B210 software-defined radio. We compare them in terms of functional compliance (3GPP NTN features, O-RAN interfaces, multi-tenancy), resource efficiency, real-time behavior, and engineering suitability. Results show that these platforms can host a joint gNB + near-RT RIC deployment using any of the considered components, although further optimizations are still required for carrier-grade performance. However, the performance and standards compliance vary significantly among them. Building on these results, we derive a decision framework that maps mission profiles and Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP) budgets to gNB/near-RT RIC combinations. Finally, we discuss the open gaps remaining before these stacks can be flown in NTN regenerative payloads.
entries.comment: 11 Pages, 6 Figures, 6 Tables. Aeroconf

entries.title: Mine Locally, Verify Globally: Exact Recovery, Compilation, and Distortion of Mined Temporal Rules
entries.abstract: Specification mining extracts temporal rules that describe relationships between events in recorded system traces. Applying these rules in distributed monitoring systems is more difficult because observations come from different nodes, whose clocks may not be synchronized, and events may be lost or reordered during transmission. In this paper, we study how to aggregate the coverage of mined rules across observers, determine whether their temporal windows are needed during monitoring, and characterize their detection under event loss. Our evaluation uses IPv6 packet traces collected from 21 receivers across four continents. We show that local mining followed by global confirmation recovers centralized rule coverage under suitable conditions while substantially reducing communication overhead. In contrast, merging traces with unaligned clocks can distort coverage by introducing incorrect temporal matches. A window-gain criterion identifies rules that require temporal state, while our loss analysis and broker experiments demonstrate why contiguous losses can be more damaging than independent losses. The results identify separate requirements for aggregating observations, selecting monitor state, and handling event loss.
entries.comment: Full version of a short paper accepted at the 28th International Conference on Distributed Computing and Networking (ICDCN 2027), Surathkal, India, January 4-7, 2027. 12 pages

entries.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
entries.abstract: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. First, we establish the S-SM-NR framework by formulating the joint design of the task graph and the transmit-listen schedule. Then, we analyze the minimum round count required by S-SM-NR and establish a connectivity condition for network localization. Subsequently, we develop a closed-form joint design that constructs the sparse task graph and the balanced transmit-listen schedule. In particular, the joint design can achieve the minimum round count under the complete physical connectivity. Finally, simulations show that the proposed S-SM-NR scheme reduces the occupied-round count and improves the localization accuracy by shortening the ranging cycle.
entries.comment: 16 pages, 14 figures, with appendices

entries.title: Can Bandits Learn to Share a Channel? Distributed Multi-Armed Bandits for Slotted ALOHA
entries.abstract: Slotted ALOHA networks constitute a playground for research on machine learning (ML)-based channel access schemes. We consider ML agents deployed in such networks and operating under severe constraints: fully distributed (independent operation), fully online (no pre-training), aperiodic (no fixed schedule), and with no explicit coordination (no signaling). We ask whether a multi-armed bandit (MAB), a minimal reinforcement learning agent, can learn the optimal policy for a capture-free slotted ALOHA system. We evaluate several MAB algorithms on aggregate network throughput and per-node fairness. Our best-performing agent is based on a Softmax bandit, which we call SALSA (Softmax ALOHA Learning for Shared Access). SALSA learns a per-node transmission policy close to optimal, with throughput near the theoretical maximum for fair random access. We achieve performance comparable to a competing state-of-the-art solution, but without requiring a priori knowledge of the network size.

entries.title: Cooperative UAV and Ground Station for Robust MEC of Dynamic Aquatic IoT: A Generative AI-Enhanced Approach
entries.abstract: The increasing aquatic Internet of Things (AIoTs) require computational support and coverage in applications such as maritime search and rescue. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can offer low-cost, flexible aerial services, and ground stations (GSs) can provide powerful supports, which can cooperate to help the AIoTs in complex scenarios. However, the collaboration between UAVs and GSs for AIoTs faces challenges of task uncertainties, AIoTs trajectory uncertainties, heterogeneities, and limited computational resources. To address these issues, we propose a cooperative UAV and GS based robust multi-access edge computing (MEC) framework to assist AIoTs in completing computational tasks. Specifically, we formulate the optimization problem of joint task offloading and UAV trajectory to minimize the total execution time, which is in the form of mixed integer nonlinear programming and NP-hard to tackle. Therefore, we propose the algorithm of generative artificial intelligence-enhanced heterogeneous agent proximal policy optimization (GAI-HAPPO). The proposed algorithm integrates GAI models to enhance the actor network ability to model complex environments and extract high-level features, thereby allowing the algorithm to predict uncertainties and adapt to dynamic conditions. Additionally, GAI stabilizes the critic network, addressing the instability of multi-agent reinforcement learning approaches. Finally, extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing benchmark methods, thus highlighting the potentials in tackling intricate, cross-domain issues in the considered scenarios.

entries.title: Conditional What-If Generation for Radio Access Network Energy under Rare and Unseen Contexts
entries.abstract: Energy-saving mechanisms in RANs must balance energy reduction and network performance under varying traffic conditions. Conditional generative models support what-if analysis by generating plausible power-consumption trajectories for radio configurations and operating scenarios, helping operators evaluate energy-saving policies before deployment. However, representative measurements are costly and operationally constrained, so historical data cover only limited configurations and conditions, leaving some contexts poorly represented or unseen during training. In this paper, we study conditional generation of RAN power-consumption trajectories under decreasing training coverage, from well-represented to rare and unseen configurations. We first introduce a context-normalized conditional generator combining temporally aligned conditioning with configuration-dependent target normalization. It improves generation for well-represented configurations but becomes less reliable as training exposure decreases because target consumption is harder to estimate. We therefore introduce a prediction-based generative framework that decomposes power consumption into global prediction, residual level and scale correction, and temporal residual generation. Experiments on a commercial 5G RAN and a public dataset show that hardware metadata provides transferable information about residual scale, while limited target observations at inference improve generation through residual-level correction without retraining. An ablation study confirms that residual-level correction provides most of the gain. Both approaches outperform state-of-the-art methods for well-represented configurations, while the prediction-based approach also generalizes to rare and unseen contexts and, with one target observation, reduces median MAE by about 50% compared with TimeWeaver.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 5 tables. Submitted for publication

entries.title: Continuum: Boundary-State-Aware Deterministic Scheduling in Dynamic LEO Networks
entries.abstract: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations support mission-critical services requiring bounded latency and predictable delivery. However, conventional snapshot-based schedulers discard the forwarding progress of unfinished time-triggered traffic across topology transitions, degrading schedulability and timing consistency. We present Continuum, aboundary-state-aware rolling-horizon scheduling framework. Continuum inherits buffered-node and arrival-time information, jointly optimizing remaining routes and transmission slots, and refines latency to improve timing consistency while preserving original timing constraints. Ablations show up to 16.6 percentage points higher schedulability from boundary-state inheritance and a 10.9-37.7 times reduction in mean jitter from joint alignment. Scalability experiments evaluate synthesis performance for workloads of up to 10K flows.

entries.title: OMNIS+: Semantic RAN Slicing and Quantization for Dynamic Split Neural Networks
entries.abstract: Edge computing enables resource-constrained devices to execute machine learning (ML) applications via task offloading, with radio access network (RAN) slicing playing a crucial role in provisioning joint communication and computing resources. However, existing RAN slicing frameworks rely on static computing models, limiting their ability to exploit dynamic semantic data representations enabled by modern neural architectures. To address this limitation, we propose OMNIS+, a semantic RAN slicing framework for multi-cell edge computing built upon a new generation of dynamic split neural models. OMNIS+ incorporates dynamic neural compression paired with adaptive quantization for task offloading, providing a versatile decision space across communication payload and compute dimensions. We leveraged a novel “box” quantization scheme that markedly enhances resilience to transmission bit errors across diverse compression rates. Considering partial system observability and distinct node objectives, we formulate two interdependent optimization problems: (i) mobile devices (MDs) maximize inference accuracy under quality-of-service (QoS) and queue-stability constraints by jointly adapting dynamic split deep neural network (DNN) branches and cell association; and (ii) each edge server (ES) allocates bandwidth, graphics processing unit (GPU) frequency, and modulation and coding scheme (MCS) to maximize the max–min inference accuracy among associated MDs under cell capacity limits. We solve these problems using a multi-agent distributed optimization framework, where MDs act as causal contextual multi-armed bandit (MAB) agents under backlog-aware Lyapunov control, while each ES executes resource allocation via block coordinate descent (BCD). Compared with state-of-the-art baselines, OMNIS+ reduces the QoS violation probability by up to 1.75 while achieving a better accuracy–violation trade-off.

entries.title: CoSlice: Coordinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 5G Network Slicing Allocation
entries.abstract: Radio Access Network (RAN) slicing is a shared resource allocation problem: each slice seeks to satisfy its Service Level Agreement (SLA) with minimal radio-resource consumption, while all slices compete for a limited resource budget. This creates both an intra-slice trade-off between SLA assurance and resource efficiency and an inter-slice conflict over shared resources, calling for specialized yet coordinated control. In this work, we present CoSlice, a coordinated multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for inter-slice physical resource block allocation in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN). CoSlice uses preference-conditioned slice agents for fast resource allocation and an LLM-based coordinator to adapt their objectives using global network observations at a slower timescale. We formulate the problem as a multi-objective partially observable stochastic game (mo-POSG), establish the existence of a Preference Correlated Equilibrium, and derive a sublinear regret bound for the learning procedure. We implement the algorithm by using a two-stage training procedure that consists of multi-objective pretraining and joint optimization. We build a network slicing evaluation environment using ORANSlice and its radio-frequency simulator (RFsim), supporting realistic protocol-stack execution and application traffic across multiple slices. Experimental results show that CoSlice reduces both average and tail SLA violations compared with other centralized and multi-agent baselines under diverse slice workloads.

entries.title: Capability Internet: A Network Architecture for Autonomous Agents
entries.abstract: Autonomous agents increasingly provide and consume network services. An agent coordinating a long-running task across organizations must track what has been done, which actions are authorized, and which provider can perform the next step. We propose Capability Internet (CI), an architecture in which agents exchange capabilities and coordinate their use through persistent tasks. Versioned descriptions specify behavior, and live instances identify the providers and resources that can supply it. Task records link each invocation to its selected instance, authority, and terms of use. When providers change, the task can reuse completed results that still meet its requirements. Five functions support capability discovery, task coordination, federated compute, intelligence reuse, and governance of capability use and settlement. Reviewed task results can supply versioned intelligence for subsequent tasks. We illustrate CI through four deployment profiles covering computing and intelligence services, manufacturing, vehicles and embodied robots, and space-ground operations, and propose an evaluation plan.
entries.comment: 9 pages, 4 figures; IEEEtran two-column preprint

entries.title: Slice Isolation-as-a-Service: An Isolation Mechanism to Proactively Defend Cross-Slice Attacks in 5G-Advanced and Beyond
entries.abstract: As cellular networks transition toward 5G-Advanced and Sixth Generation (6G) architectures, Network Slicing (NS) remains essential for multiplexing heterogeneous services over shared physical infrastructure. However, deploying critical Ultra-Reliable Low Latency Communications (URLLC) alongside standard broadband introduces severe cross-slice vulnerabilities. The implicit assumption that logical slicing inherently guarantees security fails against data plane exploits, as shared User Plane Functions (UPFs) remain susceptible to resource starvation and protocol tunneling. To address this, we propose the Slice Isolation-as-a-Service framework, which treats topological data plane isolation as an on-demand, monetizable capability. We formulate the multi-UPF resource allocation problem as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) model to strictly enforce physical and virtual isolation boundaries based on tenant security tiers, minimizing provisioning costs and end-to-end latency. To validate the framework, we engineered a novel containerized Fifth Generation (5G) testbed integrating Free5GC with Nokia Containerlab. Empirical evaluations under active volumetric flooding and the recently discovered GTP-in-GTP reflection attacks reveal that shared and Virtualized Network Function (VNF)-only isolation fail catastrophically, suffering up to 30% packet loss and complete bandwidth starvation. Our results prove that MINLP-driven strict physical isolation successfully neutralizes cross-slice injection and preserves 99.999% reliability for mission-critical slices, confirming our isolation framework as a crucial proactive defense for next-generation core networks.

entries.title: Interference-Aware Tone Selection for Bluetooth Channel Sounding
entries.abstract: Bluetooth Channel Sounding enables distance estimation using phase measurements across multiple frequencies. However, coexistence with Wi-Fi and other 2.4 GHz radios can fragment the available frequency band, making reliable ranging difficult when only a limited number of tones can be selected. Drawing on sparse antenna-array theory, we show that interference avoidance alone is insufficient: the spacing of selected tones can introduce repeated peaks in the ranging response, leading to estimation errors. We propose a lightweight, interference-aware tone-selection method that jointly considers frequency occupancy, tone spacing, and frequency span. Our method constructs a 15-tone map using a three-step rule without ranging measurements, ground-truth distance, or online candidate-map search. We evaluate the method using simulations of 900 indoor environments, a public Bluetooth Channel Sounding dataset, and measurements from commercial Nordic nRF54L15 hardware. Compared with random interference avoiding baseline, our proposed method improves ranging success percentage by 39 points under mixed interference, 29 points on the public dataset, and 82 points in hardware experiments. These results demonstrate the importance of tone selection for practical Bluetooth Channel Sounding.

entries.title: LASH-PAT: Deadlock-Free Adaptive Shortest-Path Routing for Inter-Chiplet Interconnects
entries.abstract: With the slowdown of transistor scaling, chipletbased systems, and in particular chiplet-based wafer-scale integration, have emerged as a promising approach to sustain growth in computing capability per cost for modern processors and accelerators. In recent years, many specialized inter-chiplet interconnect topologies have been proposed. In these topologies, the simple, well-established, and deadlock-free dimension-order routing scheme is not applicable due to its reliance on regular mesh structures. In this work, we study routing in these recently proposed inter-chiplet interconnect topologies by categorizing and evaluating nine deadlock-free routing functions for irregular topologies known from data center networking in this new context. This reveals a trade-off between turn-based routing, which enables path diversity, and layered routing, which ensures shortest-path delivery. To resolve this trade-off, we propose LASH-PAT, a routing function that extends layered shortestpath routing with adaptive path diversity. LASH-PAT supports multiple shortest paths and dynamically selects among them based on local congestion while preserving deadlock freedom. When compared to the best-performing baseline routing function for each combination of topology, traffic pattern, and evaluated metric, LASH-PAT improves throughput by 21.15% and reduces energy per packet by 12.77%, while providing latency comparable to the lowest-latency baseline routing function.

entries.title: Multi-connectivity in Wireless Access
entries.abstract: This paper investigates whether or not multi-connectivity, in which a User Equipment (UE) can simultaneously connect to multiple Access Points (APs), can offer a better Quality of Experience (QoE) to the users. Intuitively, multi-connectivity should offer a smoother bit rate (possibly at the expense of the average bit rate being slightly lower), so that adaptive applications can better determine at which throughput to send without introducing queueing latency. We mainly concentrate on how to share the resources of the APs amongst the UEs, modelling the lower layers via spectral efficiency and the higher layers via utility and its fluctuation. We explore various policies for resource allocation. Our results demonstrate that from the application point of view multi-connectivity is beneficial and show how to tune the parameters of the policies to obtain the best trade-off between average utility and its fluctuation.

entries.title: PAISF: A Partially Adaptive In-Order Selection Function for Routing in On-Chip, Inter-Chiplet, and Wafer-Scale Networks
entries.abstract: The growing number of compute elements per chip, along with advances such as chiplet systems and wafer-scale integration, drives the need for scalable and efficient routing algorithms for irregular topologies. A routing algorithm consists of a routing function (RF) that ensures deadlock freedom and a selection function (SF) that avoids congestion and, in some cases, guarantees in-order packet delivery. We propose two novel SFs for irregular topologies, ISF and PAISF, which ensure in-order delivery by hashing a packet's entropy value to determine its path. Packets with the same entropy follow the same path and arrive in order. Compared to a deterministic RF, a deterministic SF, and Multi, three alternative in-order delivery strategies, (PA)ISF improves throughput by 15.2% and reduces energy per packet and latency under load by 12.1% and 11.3%, at the cost of a zero-load latency increase by 3.3% on average across workloads and topologies.

entries.title: On Traffic Characterization in Time-Sensitive Networking and Deterministic Networking
entries.abstract: The traffic of an audio/video stream in IEEE Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) or an asynchronous traffic flow in IETF Deterministic Networking is specified by three parameters: an observation time interval, a maximum packet size, and a maximum number of packets in the interval. This traffic specification (TSpec) triggers three fundamental questions for TSN and DetNet: (1) if and how the traffic of a flow can be specified by these parameters after it traverses a system, (2) how to specify the traffic of a flow aggregate using the three parameters, and (3) how to use it in performance guarantee analysis. Among them, the literature has focused on (3), leaving the other two little investigated and largely open. This paper is intended to bridge the gap. Specifically, we introduce an equivalent traffic characterization for TSN TSpec, which is simple in representation and simplifies analytical development. Based on this result, we establish an output characterization property for (1) and show that the output of a TSN flow traversing a bounded-delay system can be characterized by the TSN TSpec with updated parameters. For (2) we study the superposition of TSN flows and derive TSN traffic characterizations for the aggregate of multiple TSN flows. For (3), based on a relationship between the TSN traffic characterization and the well-known token-bucket traffic characterization, backlog and delay bounds are derived. Together, these results form a calculus for TSN traffic characterization.

entries.title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
entries.abstract: Unlearning has emerged as an essential security and privacy-preserving solution in Machine Learning, enabling networks to support their clients' rights for data erasure, as mandated by data protection regulations. Introducing such a non-trivial task to an edge, highly mobile and time-sensitive vehicular network is an even greater, largely unexplored challenge. This article argues that a hierarchical Federated Unlearning approach could be aptly integrated into vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs), leveraging topology and movement to reduce communication, resource and time costs, while effectively forgetting a client's influence on the global model updates. In order to achieve this, we propose CULypso, an approximate, surgical, hierarchical unlearning algorithm tailored for clustered VANETs. Inspired by the nymph in Greek mythology, Calypso, whose name translates to 'she who conceals the knowledge', CULypso, with the capital letters referencing Clustered UnLearning, aims to achieve exactly what its name suggests: conceal, erase or forget in our case, knowledge it contains. Extensive experiments uphold the potency of our paradigm with it performing approximately 65% better than FedEraser in terms of time, server storage load, and unlearning fidelity while utterly outperforming baseline full retraining.
entries.comment: 12 pages, 14 figures

entries.title: Gateway-Free Kafka Streaming from FPGA-Based Detectors: A Bare-Metal Pipelined Producer on Zynq-7000
entries.abstract: We present a bare-metal Apache Kafka producer implemented on a Zynq-7000 System-on-Chip (SoC) for event-driven data acquisition. Events are generated in Programmable Logic (PL), transferred to the Processing System (PS) through AXI4-Stream and AXI DMA, and published to a standard Kafka broker without an intermediate gateway computer. The PS constructs ProduceRequest messages and transmits them through the lwIP raw TCP/IP API. A configurable pipeline limits the number of outstanding Kafka requests. Pipeline depths of D = 1, 2, 4, and 8 were evaluated with two independent DMA sources. For each depth, 20 independent runs of 5,000 events were acquired, for 400,000 event records in total. Each event carries a 32-bit frame counter and a 32-bit PL timestamp. PS-side instrumentation records DMA start and completion, publication, successful local tcp_write() acceptance, and reception of the corresponding Kafka acknowledgement. Measurement records are exported to a separate Kafka topic after the timed event stream has completed. Each of the 80 runs contained 5,000 records with frame values from 0 to 4,999, with no sequence discontinuities in the exported metric records and no recorded Kafka errors. Mean operational throughput was approximately 5.3 kevents/s at D = 1, 9.4-9.6 kevents/s at D = 2, 16.2 kevents/s at D = 4, and 16.8-17.5 kevents/s at D = 8. The median publish-to-acknowledgement interval was 1.62-1.64 ms at D = 1, 0.98 ms at D = 2, 0.66 ms at D = 4, and 0.83-0.86 ms at D = 8. At D = 4, the corresponding P95 values were 0.81-0.83 ms.
entries.comment: Accepted for pucblishing at IEEE Explore proceedings of ARGENCON 2026

entries.title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
entries.abstract: The effective delivery and monitoring of ICT services rely heavily on network traffic analysis. However, interpreting complex packet captures remains a challenging task that requires substantial technical expertise. Large language models (LLMs) offer promising opportunities to automate network traffic in- vestigation, yet their reliability in packet-level field extraction and flow-level sequence reconstruction remains an open research question. This study proposes a reproducible, question-answering- based evaluation methodology to assess the capabilities of LLMs in network trace analysis. Using real-world benign traffic from the CICIDS2017 dataset, we evaluate multiple models against a human-generated ground truth, comparing their performance on raw textual traffic dumps and protocol-filtered representations. Model responses are assessed through an automated LLM- as-a-judge pipeline, validated against human evaluations. The results demonstrate that protocol filtering significantly reduces prompt overhead while improving answer accuracy by reducing incorrect responses. These findings highlight the importance of protocol-aware traffic filtering as an effective optimization for improving the efficiency and reliability of LLM-assisted network management.
entries.comment: This publication has been submitted to NOMS2027

entries.title: HiGAI-Net: Hierarchical Encrypted Traffic Classification for Generative AI Services
entries.abstract: The Radio Access Network (RAN) today does not have a reliable way to identify GenAI traffic (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, or Google Gemini traffic) at the bearer level. TLS 1.3 moves SNI into the encrypted handshake record, and Encrypted ClientHello (ECH) removes it entirely from passive inspection; Gemini has partly shifted to QUIC where SNI visibility also depends on whether ECH is deployed. Without per-flow application identity, differentiated QoS for GenAI services is not possible. HiGAI-Net tackles this using only packet-header metadata, stacking three independently trained classifiers: a binary AI/Non-AI gate (98.5% weighted F1), a per-service resolver across ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini (86.4%), and a text-vs-voice/video mode classifier (61.0%). The core innovation is a suite of sliding-window temporal features that track how DL/UL byte-ratios evolve within a session – the per-quarter and per-half ratio trends, a trend differential ΔR, and a streaming regularity index. Tested on 44,492 labeled flows, gradient-boosted tree models consistently outperformed all deep-learning variants; a per-flow label cache brings amortised inference below 1 μs per packet.
entries.comment: Paper accepted in IEEE Globecom 2026

entries.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
entries.abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). Using agentic coding techniques, SL is implemented in two O-RAN-compliant packages, reducing development time by 400 times (2 h 40 min [OCUDU] vs. 6.5 weeks [OAI]), 228-fold fewer human prompts (4 vs. 913), and less than half the tokens (0.64B vs. 1.43B). An associated end-to-end framework, SLED, is implemented to establish per-sensor radio and network isolation across edge, campus, and remote high-performance computing (HPC) tiers. Over-the-air wireless experiments demonstrate that while conventional network slicing causes critical delays to increase more than 2,300-fold under high traffic load, SLED maintains stable latency. Scaling evaluations on the two RAN stacks show that throughput remains within 0.9% and 1.4% of expected allocations even as the number of sensor slices increases. The results demonstrate that SLED preserves latency-critical telemetry while effectively utilizing resources across the sensor-to-HPC pipeline. The SLED software and evaluation datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/UNL-CPN-Lab/SLED-Sensor-SLicing-from-Edge-to-Datacenter.
entries.comment: Accepted in IEEE Annual Congress on Artificial Intelligence of Things (IEEE AIoT) 2026. The SLED software and evaluation datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/UNL-CPN-Lab/SLED-Sensor-SLicing-from-Edge-to-Datacenter

entries.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
entries.abstract: This study proposes an interesting approach for vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communication, which integrates blockchain technology, federated learning (FL), and allocation optimization of latency and resources. The research evaluates the proposed system using various performance metrics such as packet delivery ratio (PDR), model accuracy, and latency and demonstrates its superiority over existing techniques. Furthermore, the system provides enhanced security through consensus optimization and k-anonymity for data privacy. Overall, the proposed system is a promising solution for efficient and secure V2V communication in the era of connected and autonomous vehicles. Moreover, the proposed approach achieves higher reliability, lower latency, and better resource utilization compared to traditional 5G.
entries.journalRef: GLOBECOM 2023 - 2023 IEEE Global Communications Conference, pp. 1302-1307

entries.title: ASCEND: Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design
entries.abstract: Designing resilient and cost-effective IP network topologies over an existing physical infrastructure is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly at large scale and under extensive failure modeling assumptions. Traditional deterministic approaches struggle to jointly address resiliency against shock (large customer-impact outages) and implementation cost objectives when the number of candidate circuits grows quadratically with the number of sites to be interconnected. In this paper, we propose Automated Shockproof Cost-Efficient Network Design (ASCEND), a systematic design pipeline for IP core network optimization based on a two-level optimization framework. At the outer level, ASCEND uses Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) to select core sites and core circuits. Given a core design, the inner-level integral Multi-Commodity Flow (MCF) formulation selects edge circuits and maps both core and edge circuits onto optical (fiber/transport) paths while prioritizing resource disjointness and latency. Network designs are evaluated using two competing objectives: a performance cost capturing resiliency under probabilistic failure scenarios and an implementation cost. The performance cost incorporates an exponentially weighted vulnerability metric that explicitly penalizes infeasible configurations. Experimental results on multiple real-world networks demonstrate that ASCEND consistently identifies designs that outperform a manually engineered baseline in both resiliency and implementation cost.
entries.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management

entries.title: Fundamental Tradeoffs in Sampling, Transmission and Information Freshness: Instantaneous Feedback
entries.abstract: We study a time-slotted generate-at-will status-update system over an erasure channel with transmission success probability q, subject to average sampling- and transmission-rate constraints f_s and f_r, respectively. The sampler-transmitter pair jointly decides whether to idle, retransmit a stale packet, or replace it with a fresh sample. We derive a universal lower bound on the optimal average age of information, analyze a class of stationary randomized policies, and obtain an optimal policy within this class that provides a 4-approximation guarantee. The joint problem reduces to the sampling-constrained problem when f_s≤qf_r and the transmission-constrained problem when f_s≥f_r. For qf_r<f_s<f_r, we formulate a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) and introduce the class Π of (W,R) policies, where W specifies a waiting threshold for transmission and R specifies a packet-replacement threshold. We prove that, for every choice of Lagrange multipliers, the corresponding Lagrangian-relaxed Markov decision process admits an optimal policy in Π. We then formulate a linear program (LP) over distributions of (W,R) policies and prove that choosing a policy according to an optimal LP solution yields an optimal CMDP policy. Moreover, there exists an optimal LP solution assigning positive probability to at most three (W,R) policies. Since Π is countably infinite, for every ε>0 we construct a finite subset Π_ε⊂Π and show that the LP restricted to this set yields an ε-optimal policy. Finally, we derive a stronger pair of lower bounds by considering systems with only the sampling-rate or transmission-rate constraint. Using these bounds, we construct a policy randomizing among four (W,R) policies with a 2-approximation guarantee for qf_r<f_s<f_r.

entries.title: Post-Quantum Migration of Wi-Fi Key Establishment: A Hybrid ML-KEM Design for OWE and FILS, Validated on OWE with hostapd
entries.abstract: The key agreements that protect a Wi-Fi connection rely on Diffie-Hellman, which a sufficiently capable quantum computer would break; an adversary can therefore record an association today and decrypt its traffic years later. Key establishment is thus the part of IEEE 802.11 that has to be migrated first. This work targets the two protocols that perform that agreement inside the frames used to set up the link: Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE), which encrypts otherwise open networks, and Fast Initial Link Setup (FILS), designed for fast connection in dense and mobile deployments. We propose replacing their Diffie-Hellman exchange with a hybrid one that runs the classical elliptic-curve agreement alongside ML-KEM (FIPS 203) and derives the master key from both secrets, so the connection stays protected as long as either component remains unbroken. The exchange reuses the frames each protocol already sends and adds no extra round trip; an access point can advertise the hybrid mode alongside classical OWE, and a station configured to require it refuses to associate without a completed post-quantum exchange. Binding the advertised capabilities to the derived key is specified as a design extension and is not part of the prototype. We validate the design with a working implementation on hostapd and wpa_supplicant: both endpoints derive the same key in every measured connection, with the two smaller parameter sets each enlarged association frame fits in a single frame even under a conservative 1500-byte fragmentation threshold, and the added connection time and computation stay below half a millisecond. The measurements are obtained on OWE; the design carries over to FILS, whose frame budget is left for specific measurement. Of the three ML-KEM parameter sets, the intermediate one offers the best balance between security level and size.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 4 tables

entries.title: Network Intrusion Detection Adaptability under Spurious Labels: A Noise-Aware Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning Framework
entries.abstract: Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDSs) must incrementally adapt to emerging attacks, even when only a limited amount of labeled network traffic is available. Consequently, Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning (FSCIL)-based NIDSs have gained growing attention. However, existing FSCIL-based NIDSs are highly vulnerable to label noise in newly-observed attack classes. To address this limitation, we propose NAFN, a noise-aware FSCIL-based NIDS framework that reduces the impact of mislabeled data during incremental adaptation. NAFN consists of two components: (i) Noise Detection, which identifies and removes mislabeled biflows using noise-detection algorithms, and (ii) Feature Sampling, which estimates class-conditional embeddings from clean biflows, calibrates them with base-class statistics, and resamples synthetic features to recover the original biflow count. The framework follows the Rethink Few-Shot (RFS) teacher-student paradigm with lightweight nearest-neighbor or logistic regression classifiers, and various pretraining & memory selection strategies. Experiments on CSE-CIC-IDS2018, Edge-IIoT, and IoT-NID datasets show that NAFN effectively preserves prior knowledge and maintains strong incremental performance even under 50% label noise, consistently improving new-class F1-scores over non-denoised baselines, up to +52%, while being time-efficient and robust in cross-network and high-noise incremental settings. The implementation is publicly available to foster reproducibility.
entries.journalRef: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management 2026

entries.title: An Alternative to Crawlers: Scalable P2P Network Monitoring Using the Network Scale-Up Method
entries.abstract: p2p networks have remained an active area of research and development for decades. Originally used for data dissemination, they have later become instrumental to decentralized payment systems, blockchains, and Web3 applications. Since decentralization is a crucial property of these networks, they are continuously monitored to track attributes such as the geographical distribution of nodes, which serve as indicators of infrastructure concentration and resilience. However, monitoring typically relies on network crawls to derive accurate snapshots, which requires substantial computational and network resources. In contrast, nsum is a statistical tool that estimates the prevalence of subpopulations based on responses to questions such as How many people do you know in a specific group? This work leverages the information embedded in Kademlia routing tables to develop a lightweight nsum-based measurement and estimation framework that infers global network attribute distributions from a small set of nodes, offering an alternative to full-network crawls. As a case study, we evaluate our approach on ipfs, a well-researched and widely used Web3 data storage and retrieval network. This is the first application of nsum to decentralized network measurement. We evaluate our methodology on two datasets: the first comprises 360 full-network crawls collected over one month to assess our measurement-estimation approach across multiple simulated measurement scenarios, while the second dataset was collected through a deployment of the proposed lightweight measurement framework during May 2026. The results show that local Kademlia routing views, with only 10 nodes, preserve sufficient information to accurately estimate global attribute distributions, achieving normalized biases below 10 and closely tracking temporal changes in network composition.
entries.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures

entries.title: Adaptive Wake-on-Radio Communication for Batteryless IoT Systems
entries.abstract: Batteryless Internet of Things (IoT) systems powered by energy harvesting require communication mechanisms that dynamically adapt to fluctuating energy availability while maintaining ultra-low-power operation. This paper presents a Wake-on-Radio (WoR) communication framework for low-power intermittent IoT systems in which the node's communication state adapts to its stored energy. The framework uses a batteryless IoT node that integrates a photovoltaic harvester, a 570 μF capacitor, two voltage supervisors, and a microcontroller. The voltage supervisors drive an energy-aware finite state machine that switches the node between Shutdown, Low-Power Listening (LPL), Transmit, and Receive modes. The proposed system employs the integrated WoR capability of the transceiver, eliminating the need for additional wake-up hardware. For the evaluated traffic conditions and an LPL wake-up rate of 16 Hz, the measured power consumption is approximately 1.2 μW in the Shutdown mode, 300 μW during LPL, 531 μW for reception, and 627 μW for transmission. System-level experiments under solar-harvesting operation validate the proposed framework, demonstrating reliable bidirectional communication with no packet losses observed across repeated runs at a harvested input power of 1.2 mW.
entries.comment: This is an open-access, author-archived version of a manuscript published in ApplePies 2026 Conference

entries.title: Disaggregated LLM Inference in Space: A Communication Feasibility Study
entries.abstract: Orbital data centers could enable large-scale AI inference, but efficiently serving a frontier language model to many users may require several compute satellites to cooperate over optical links. While disaggregated inference, which splits large language model (LLM) serving across machines, is well established in terrestrial data centers, its viability under the unique constraints of orbital deployments remains an open question. This article investigates how link capacity and satellite separation affect two types of disaggregated LLM serving, in both compact satellite formations and distributed constellations. Prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) migrates a large KV cache once per request, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) exchanges small activations at every mixture-of-experts layer for every generated token. The two respond to distance in different ways. PDD is limited mainly by link capacity and, with fast enough links, tolerates separations of up to a thousand kilometers. AFD is limited mainly by propagation delay, which accumulates layer by layer and forces attention and expert instances within about a kilometer of each other. Based on these results, we propose a hierarchical orbital inference architecture and provide network design guidelines for future orbital data centers, including the role of ground access latency.

entries.title: Early UAV Detection Using 5G NR LEO Downlinks for Passive ISAC
entries.abstract: 5G New Radio (NR) low-Earth-orbit (LEO) downlinks enable passive integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) detection. Weak echoes require motion-compensated accumulation, but exhaustive searches postpone alerts. We propose a receiver that combines selective Doppler-rate search, early UAV alerts and continued delay-Doppler estimation. Classical, statistical and neural configurations select rates of Doppler change to search, while a shared correlation score determines detection. Simulated echo delay, Doppler and power follow the moving satellite-UAV-receiver geometry, propagation loss, assumed scattering and antenna response. In a line-of-sight scene with acquired beams and UAVs at 5-8 km horizontal distance, all three configurations match exhaustive search at 92.9% correct final detections, with 0.10-0.13% observed false alerts on no-UAV recordings. The neural configuration reduces mean time to the first correct alert by 36.5% versus exhaustive search and 21.9% versus the closest literature baseline, averaging over successfully detected UAVs. These results demonstrate earlier UAV alerts while preserving exhaustive search's final detection accuracy, supporting passive sensing over cellular satellites.

entries.title: Prediction-Driven Contract Matching with Controlled Overbooking for Cloud-Edge DDoS Scrubbing Markets
entries.abstract: Cloud-edge distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) scrubbing requires ex-ante capacity commitments under uncertain traffic, heterogeneous budgets, resource costs, and fulfillment risks. We develop a prediction-driven two-stage contracting mechanism coordinating business entities (BEs), edge scrubbing nodes (ESs), and a cloud scrubbing center (CS) through BE-ES (B&E) main-service and ES-CS (E&C) supplementary contracts. In the first offline phase, Transformer forecasts generate candidate reserved scrubbing rates, generalized Nash bargaining determines candidate prices, and interim many-to-one B&E matching permits controlled overbooking under scenario-based aggregate ES shortfall-risk assessment. In the second offline phase, formal E&C reservations are established subject to capacity and payment constraints; their finalized rates and prices update ES-side proxy scores and guide localized risk-aware B&E contract adjustment. During online fulfillment, an edge-first, cloud-assisted weighted proportional allocation policy allocates scrubbing capacity under finalized contracts without rematching, renegotiation, or additional cloud reservations. Experiments with CICDDoS2019-derived workloads show that the proposed mechanism satisfies the prescribed empirical shortfall-risk criterion across all 100 evaluated horizon-instance pairs, whereas the NoRisk ablation violates it in all 100. Runtime measurements indicate lightweight online fulfillment relative to offline contract formation. The evaluated configurations also exhibit limited overall scrubbing coverage and near-zero realized cloud utilization.
entries.comment: 22 pages, 5 figures, including supplementary material

entries.title: Design Rules for Low-Latency Multipath Congestion Control
entries.abstract: We first study optimal congestion control from a theoretical perspective. Concretely, we consider a system that optimizes the sum of the utilities of all the users, in which the users are allowed to send their traffic over different paths over the network and derive design rules that optimal (low-latency) multipath congestion control needs to follow. Because, as it turns out that optimal congestion control requires coordination between the network nodes, and hence, is hard to implement, we investigate how to approximate its performance with algorithms in which (i) the network nodes make independent decisions and (ii) coordination is only allowed between the subflows that belong to the same user. Therefore, these design rules need to be slightly relaxed. We compare the performance of these realistic algorithms with the optimal algorithm. We also investigate to what extent the algorithms that are currently defined and are being defined in the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF), in particular, (i) Prague congestion control (i.e., congestion control based on Accurate Explicit Congestion Notification (AccECN) marks) and (ii) a variant of a loss-based multipath congestion control algorithm, adhere to these rules.

entries.title: VISTA: A Framework for Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness
entries.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming intelligent transportation systems by connecting roadside cameras, edge computing units, vehicles, and traffic infrastructure into a shared sensing and decision-making ecosystem. However, transmitting raw traffic video over vehicle-to-everything (V2X) links is bandwidth-intensive, while deploying large multimodal models directly on resource-constrained vehicles is often impractical. To address these limitations, this article proposes VISTA (Vision-Informed Semantic Traffic Awareness), a multimodal vision-language edge-intelligence framework that combines predictive video representation learning with lightweight language-based reasoning to provide communication-efficient traffic situational awareness. In the proposed architecture, roadside surveillance units employ the Video Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (V-JEPA) and an attentive-pooler module to convert traffic video clips into compact future-scene embeddings. These embeddings are transmitted through V2X links to vehicle-mounted systems, where a TinyLlama small language model, enhanced with a custom visual adapter, interprets the embeddings alongside natural-language (NL) traffic queries. VISTA enables vehicles to obtain interpretable traffic information, reason about upcoming scene dynamics, and identify potential collision risks without receiving raw video streams. Experimental results in a digital-twin urban traffic environment show that VISTA achieves 97.77% accuracy and an 89% F1 score for future collision prediction while reducing the communication payload by several orders of magnitude compared with raw RGB video transmission. These results demonstrate the feasibility of embedding-based multimodal intelligence for low-latency, communication-efficient, and safety-oriented IoT-enabled transportation systems.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, Accepted for publication in IEEE Internet of Things Magazine, 2026

entries.title: IZM-DSR: A New Zone-Disjoint Multi-path Routing Algorithm for Mobile Ad-Hoc Network
entries.abstract: Some of multi-path routing algorithms in MANETs use multiple paths simultaneously. These algorithms can attempt to find node-disjoint to achieve higher fault tolerance. By using node-disjoint paths, it is expected that the end-to-end delay in each case should be independent of each other. However, because of natural properties and medium access mechanisms in ad hoc networks, such as CSMA/CA, the endto-end delay between any source and destination depends on the pattern of communication in the neighborhood region. In this case some of the intermediate nodes should be silent to reverence their neighbors and this matter increases the end-toend delay. To avoid this problem, multi-path routing algorithms can use zone-disjoint paths instead of node-disjoint paths. In this paper we propose a new multi-path routing algorithm that selects zone-disjoint paths, using omnidirectional antenna. We evaluate our algorithm in several different scenarios. The simulation results show that our approach is very effective in decreasing routing overhead and end-to-end delay.

entries.title: Diagnosis as Percolation on an Evidence Graph: Root-Cause Recoverability in Network Fault Diagnosis
entries.abstract: Diagnosing failures from incomplete observations presents three challenges: determining whether sufficient evidence connects a possible cause to a symptom, distinguishing the true cause from plausible alternatives, and assessing when a diagnosis can be trusted. We introduce an evidence-graph framework that separates these challenges and uses percolation theory to analyze how missing information affects cause-symptom connectivity. In controlled simulations with an average degree of four, a giant connected component emerges when approximately 25% of evidence is retained, but a specific cause-alarm pair reaches 50% connectivity only after slightly more than half is retained. Even connectivity does not guarantee correct cause identification. We apply this framework to multi-LLM diagnosis of IEEE 802.11 packet captures. A final reconciliation pass improves evidence-grounding weighted F1 from 0.912 to 0.964, primarily by removing isolated citations rather than connecting previously separate evidence chains, consistently across three graph constructions. However, connectivity is not a reliable confidence measure: its association with diagnostic quality becomes statistically insignificant after controlling for capture length, citation count, within-capture dependence, and multiple comparisons. Further experiments show that directed and weighted edges help selectively, while simpler overlap measures or domain-specific methods sometimes perform better. These findings establish evidence graphs as a framework for separating evidence availability, causal distinguishability, and confidence reliability, while demonstrating that connected evidence alone cannot certify diagnostic correctness.
entries.comment: 28 pages, 8 figures, 20 tables

entries.title: Sustaining In-Network Computation in Satellite Networks: An Architecture for Semantic Continuity
entries.abstract: Satellite computations often outlast the paths and providers initially serving them. We argue that in-network computing should organize changing execution opportunities around one continuing logical computation: workers execute ready operations, while consumers recognize which results already contribute. We present an architecture separating logical computation, stream context, and physical binding, and show in wildfire assessment how retained observations support recomputation while reachable association history stays in place. A 300-node Linux prototype examines placement, dependency assembly, and continuation. Across 120 images, stage-wise placement delivers 82.08% of positions within deadlines versus 76.06% for single-node placement, while traces separate blocked output delivery from dependencies split across providers. Across 50 observations with 20-node isolation, Confirmation-Coordinated Rebinding (CCR) coordinates replanning, source replay, cross-attempt acceptance, and in-band confirmation to complete all 50 observations with verified outputs using seven replays and 13 ignored duplicate outputs.
entries.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications

entries.title: SliceWise: Traffic-Aware Multi-Agent RL with Temporal Encoding for Joint Slice Admission and Resource Orchestration in O-RAN
entries.abstract: Ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC) services in mission-critical applications such as industrial automation, remote healthcare, and autonomous systems demand stringent quality-of-service (QoS) guarantees under dynamic, resource-constrained wireless conditions. Open radio access networks (O-RAN) offer a software-defined and programmable foundation for embedding AI-driven control. This letter proposes SliceWise, a traffic-aware multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for joint admission control, user-slice association, and resource orchestration in O-RAN. The control problem is modeled as a cooperative multi-agent Markov decision process, with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks capturing temporal traffic dynamics and dueling double deep Q-networks (D3QN) ensuring stable learning. Simulation results show that SliceWise substantially reduces delay violations and packet drops while improving slice-level reliability and resource efficiency, offering a scalable orchestration solution for AI-native O-RAN deployments.

entries.title: EdgeNet City: Context-Aware AI-RAN Planning toward Autonomous Urban Connectivity
entries.abstract: The evolution from 5G toward 6G calls for more anticipatory and context-aware Cell-on-Wheels (COW) planning in wireless networks. We present EdgeNet City, an online framework that grounds free-form natural-language inputs in geographic activity representations and path-gain data. A catalog-referenced representation links activity roles, geographic features and predefined demand profiles, separating semantic selection from deterministic spatial computation. The algorithm combines prescribed demand with relative propagation support to screen service areas for subsequent COW assessment. We publicly release a London dataset with 22,678 transmitters, approximately 449.4 billion path-gain records and retained receiver geometry. Within prepared propagation domains, the online prototype reuses these records without new ray tracing or live operator measurements. In a matched 20-event study across six London environments, the expanded representation increases mean spatial overlap with the reused full technical-review reference from 0.4929 for the single-feature Venue-only baseline to 0.7203. Rule-based and language-model planners select identical activities in this panel. With need-aware ranking and a three-cell diagnostic budget fixed, the expanded representation increases mean Reference-need Capture by 25.44 percentage points over Venue-only.
entries.comment: 6 pages. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 (Mobile and Wireless Networks). Author manuscript

entries.title: Feedback-Aware Residual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Timely Communication in Cognitive Radio Networks
entries.abstract: Supporting time-sensitive services in cognitive radio networks requires distributed access strategies that translate shared spectrum opportunities into timely packet delivery. Achieving this objective is challenging because reception conditions are only partially observable to individual transmitters, while dynamic competition and access overhead constrain the service that can be completed within packet deadlines. We formulate a distributed access problem that captures the coupling among interference-dependent reception, queue evolution, and protocol durations. To address this problem, we propose feedback-aware residual multi-agent proximal policy optimization (FAR-MAPPO) under centralized training and decentralized execution. The method constructs channel-specific historical feedback representations that complement instantaneous sensing with evidence from completed access attempts. A residual policy network integrates this experience with current observations and packet urgency to guide local access decisions. Numerical results show improved timely delivery over the baseline methods, particularly under heavy traffic and bursty arrivals with mixed packet deadlines.

entries.title: Budgeted Decision-Model-Guided Joint-Action Search for Satellite Edge Computing
entries.abstract: Efficient task offloading in satellite edge computing requires coordinated allocation of communication and computing resources. Search methods based on large language models (LLMs) have been shown to generate high-quality resource allocations, but the latency of individual model requests and repeated model interactions can lead to substantial solver overhead. We propose budgeted joint-action search (BJAS), an integrated decision-model-guided solver that jointly optimizes satellite offloading and power allocation to minimize average task-completion latency under explicit search budgets. Its bounded candidate pools combine single-terminal updates with power-inheriting offload replacements for batched selection, retaining two-terminal coordination without enumerating additional power vectors. Across 60 completed runs per method under the workflows' respective configurations, BJAS reduces mean total solver time by 97.16% relative to LLM-generated offloading while achieving a mean task-completion latency close to that of the LLM baseline. BJAS also achieves lower mean task-completion latency than the tested genetic algorithm and deep deterministic policy gradient baselines.
entries.comment: 6 pages. Submitted to IEEE ICC 2027 (SAC: Satellite and Space Communications). Author manuscript

entries.title: Wireless Edge-Assisted Adaptive Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models in Physical AI
entries.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models enable embodied artificial intelligence (AI) by translating visual observations and language instructions into robotic actions. Emerging use cases in physical AI are expected to drive the need for efficient inference and communication, as the computational demands of the VLA models pose challenges for real-time control with limited onboard resources. Test-time scaling through latent reasoning allows these models to refine hidden representations without generating explicit chain-of-thought (CoT) tokens, but introduces a trade-off between task success, inference latency, and energy consumption. In this paper, we address the efficient collaborative inference under a realistic communication scenario. We propose a wireless edge-assisted framework for adaptive latent reasoning (WEALR) that augments onboard computation with edge computing. A decision-making agent jointly selects the execution location and latent-reasoning convergence threshold. We formulate this joint adaptation as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP). A Lagrangian-constrained deep reinforcement learning (CDRL) approach, namely trust region policy optimization Lagrangian (TRPO-Lag), learns to balance task performance and resource consumption under varying wireless conditions and task requirements. We evaluate the framework using LIBERO manipulation tasks, profiled VLA inference costs, and ray-traced wireless channels. Experimental results demonstrate that TRPO-Lag achieves up to 23% higher feasibility-weighted task success rate compared to benchmark CDRL methods.
entries.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, submitted to IEEE ICC

entries.title: RF-Based Macronutrient Estimation in Liquid Foods via Composition-Aware Multi-Task Learning
entries.abstract: Current approaches to macronutrient estimation range from high-overhead laboratory analysis to user-dependent methods such as manual nutritional lookup, reading package labels, and vision-based image analysis. These approaches are often time-consuming, input-dependent, or sensitive to imaging and measurement conditions. In this work, we investigate synchronous 2.4 GHz OFDM radio-frequency (RF) measurements for estimating carbohydrate, fat, and protein content in liquid foods. Using a controlled sensing setup, we study how liquid composition shapes frequency-domain RF responses – a first step toward a sensor integrated into a liquid-contacting vessel that estimates macronutrient content passively and label-free, and toward composition-aware RF food analysis beyond liquids. We propose the Ingredient-Conditioned OFDM Transformer (ICOT), a structure-aware multi-task Transformer that operates on two-dimensional OFDM channel frequency response matrices. ICOT infers canonical ingredient categories representing dielectric-driver composition and uses them to condition macronutrient regression through feature concatenation. On 28,420 captures spanning 55 beverage classes, ICOT achieves an in-distribution MAE of 0.101 g/100 ml and an out-of-distribution MAE of 0.485 g/100 ml – comparable in magnitude to deviations present in manufacturer-reported labels – though generalization to novel formulations remains the primary open challenge.

entries.title: Stargate: Security Analysis and Mission-Aware Firewall for the CubeSat Space Protocol
entries.abstract: The CubeSat Space Protocol (CSP) is widely used for communication in CubeSat missions, yet its security model and attack surface remain largely unexplored. In this work, we present a systematic security analysis of CSP and identify fundamental limitations in its trust assumptions, coarse-grained network abstractions, privileged management services, application command semantics, and lack of mission-context awareness. Based on these findings, we develop a taxonomy of CSP attacks spanning four classes: network identity abuse, management service abuse, application semantic abuse, and mission context abuse. We then introduce Stargate, a modular, mission-aware firewall that enforces CSP-specific policies derived from this taxonomy, including node and service authorization, command-level filtering, and mission-context constraints. We implement Stargate and evaluate it on a virtual testbed based on a real-world CubeSat mission and flight software. Stargate successfully blocks all 11 representative attacks across the four attack classes while introducing only 1.42 ms of additional median round-trip latency. Our results demonstrate that protocol- and mission-aware policy enforcement provides a practical approach for securing CSP-based spacecraft networks.
entries.comment: To be published at the 1st IEEE International Conference on Resilience and Integrated Security for Space and Critical Systems proceedings
